intention: When a shim receives a bus message it has no handler for, it bounces it back to the sender. The sender's handle_bounce (BaseShim fallback) raises a trouble ticket. Devices that have grown capacity to deal with returned mail override handle_bounce.
why: The sender owns the decision about what to do with returned mail, not the receiver or the bus (Law 6). A sender with capacity to handle bounces should be able to use that capacity. The base class fallback is the safety net, not the ceiling.
falsifier: Send a bus message to a device with no handler for that verb. The message bounces to sender. The sender's handle_bounce fires and a trouble ticket appears. Then override handle_bounce on a test device — the override fires instead of the default trouble raise.

gates_bound.build: BaseShim gains handle_bounce (fallback: raise trouble), deliver() bounces instead of raising, bounce envelope carries is_bounce guard
gates_bound.proof: bounce fires on unknown verb, trouble ticket raised by default handle_bounce, override handle_bounce suppresses trouble

traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth)
Law 6 (the sender owns the decision about what to do with returned mail)

watchme.trigger: when a bus message is sent to a device with no handler
watchme.enough: 3 bounces observed in live operation with correct sender attribution
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier
